parsed.summary: The main theorem is formalized faithfully. For n ≥ 1, if S ⊂ ℝⁿ is convex and compact, has nonempty interior and barycenter 0, and int(S) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}, then vol(S) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!. Two companion lemmas compute the barycenter (0) and the volume ((n+1)ⁿ/n!) of the centered simplex (n+1)Δₙ − (1,…,1). The most important caveat is that the sharpness existence theorem `exists_centeredBody_sharp` carries the false hypothesis (1 : ℕ) = 0, so it is vacuous. Also, nothing formalizes that the centered simplex has 0 as its only interior lattice point, so sharpness is not actually established.

glossary.standard_concept: affine map defining the centered simplex

glossary.plain: Lebesgue volume of K, as a real number (toReal; 0 if the volume is infinite)
glossary.note: The name says 'normalized', but this is plain Lebesgue volume. It is finite for compact K.
Junk values occur only when vol = 0 or the integral is not integrable. Both are excluded for compact sets with nonempty interior.

glossary.plain: a convex, compact set with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and int ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}

lean_claims.plain: For n > 0 and S ⊂ ℝⁿ: if S is convex and compact, int S ≠ ∅, the barycenter of S is 0, and int S ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}, then vol(S) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
For all n, the barycenter of (n+1)Δₙ − (1,…,1) is 0.
Assuming 1 = 0 in ℕ (false), for n > 0 there is a centered body of volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!. The statement is vacuous.

paper_claims.plain: Let K ⊂ ℝⁿ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with barycenter 0 and int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}. Then vol(K) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
The simplex (n+1)Δₙ − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0, has no interior lattice point other than 0, and has volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

coverage.why: The hypotheses and conclusion match. n > 0 is implicit in the paper.
The false hypothesis 1 = 0 makes the existence claim vacuous. The two separate simplex lemmas cover the barycenter and the volume, but not the lattice-point condition.

flags.explanation: The hypothesis hbase : (1 : ℕ) = 0 is false, so the theorem holds vacuously and says nothing about the existence of an extremal body.
flags.probe_idea: Prove `example : ¬ ((1:ℕ) = 0) := by decide` to confirm vacuity. Then restate the theorem without hbase.

flags.explanation: No target theorem asserts that the centered simplex is convex, compact, has nonempty interior, or satisfies int ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}. Sharpness of the bound is therefore not formally established.

lint_verdicts.why: In every use the set is compact with nonempty interior (or is the bounded simplex), so the volume is positive and finite and x is integrable on the set.
